cases.description: A valid scoped dispute blocks a static direct claim even when independent context-independent acceptances satisfy every positive requirement.
A context-independent claim opts into the endorsed policy and has independent accepted referential and scholarly reviews.
Eligible reviews cannot flatten a claim that does not name the endorsed policy.
One accepted dimension is insufficient when the policy requires both referential and scholarly acceptance.
An otherwise sufficient review set is blocked by an active dispute covered by the policy veto rule.
Source silence can remain in the research-claims view but cannot produce a context-free endorsed triple.
Permanent supersession remains effective after the successor expires unless an explicit reinstatement event occurs.
A suspension hides only the named predecessor during the suspension interval and then releases it.
A community review representing several communities is unauthorized unless referenced mandates cover every one of them.
